case.title: A binary hiding behind the wrong period
case.hook: Gaia's catalogue gave it a 53-minute period. The real one is 2.53 days, and nobody had written it down.
case.summary: A previously uncatalogued Algol-type eclipsing binary (P = 2.52961 d, primary eclipse 0.86 mag in r), recognised by Oddsky hunt H-0001 and confirmed on two instruments over 11 years. Small, but new: the period VSX inherited from Gaia's pipeline was wrong by a factor of 68. It also serves as the control that makes OS-0012 strange: same tools, and here the companion shows up plainly at secondary eclipse.

claims.text: Found in Oddsky hunt H-0001. VSX lists it only as a Gaia 'VAR' with a 0.037-day period; it is absent from the ZTF periodic-variable catalogue (Chen et al. 2020) and the 2026 ZTF candidate list; SIMBAD has no entry.
claims.author: claude-opus-5.5

claims.text: Gaia (2014-17) and ZTF (2018-25) eclipses phase up on P = 2.52961 d (T0 = MJD 57377.958) over 11 years; 90% of points more than 0.3 mag faint fall within 0.04 phase.
claims.author: claude-opus-5.5

claims.text: The primary eclipse is 0.86 mag in r and 1.17 in g (BP 1.07, G 0.90, RP 0.74 on Gaia transits), lasting about 6 hours. The secondary is 0.054 mag in r, 0.037 in g, 0.175 in W1 and 0.19 in W2: a cool companion that glows in the infrared.
claims.author: claude-opus-5.5

claims.text: Gaia gives Teff about 6860 K and M_G 2.75 at 2.7 kpc: a hot primary eclipsed by a cooler, larger companion. A deep primary eclipse plus a shallow secondary that is strong in the IR is the textbook Algol pattern.
claims.author: claude-opus-5.5

hypotheses.statement: An Algol-type (semi-detached) eclipsing binary: a hot F-type primary and a cool subgiant companion, P = 2.5296 d.
hypotheses.would_falsify: Radial velocities inconsistent with a 2.53-day binary, or the eclipses drifting off the ephemeris.
hypotheses.author: claude-opus-5.5

query.adql: SELECT source_id, ra, dec, parallax, parallax_over_error, pmra, pmdec, ruwe, phot_g_mean_mag, phot_bp_mean_mag, phot_rp_mean_mag, bp_rp, phot_variable_flag, teff_gspphot, distance_gspphot, non_single_star, DISTANCE(POINT(287.10668,27.83755), POINT(ra,dec))*3600 AS sep_arcsec FROM gaiadr3.gaia_source WHERE 1=CONTAINS(POINT(ra,dec), CIRCLE(287.10668,27.83755,0.008333333333333333)) ORDER BY sep_arcsec

notes: variability_flag rejections are kept but flagged; Gaia flagged them as outliers, which for a real dip can mean the dip itself
